brief: Goldman's trading desks read late-August positioning as low but stable heading into a payrolls print that some expect to be the second consecutive negative one. Hedge funds re-grossed modestly while nets stayed flat and historically low, fundamental long/short net leverage at the 3rd percentile of one year, and long onlys showed no re-risking. The non-economic bid from CTAs, corporates and retail is still running, at reduced speed, into thin summer liquidity, and sentiment has decayed to neutral-to-bearish while fundamental investors hesitate to chase. Pierre Sabourealt adds those two together and gets, all else equal, a fairly resilient tape. Supporting flows: EPFR global equity funds took +$9bn against +$40bn the prior week with US funds in outflow, institutions very slightly sold S&P futures, CTAs bought $2.1bn to $147bn length with about $2bn more forecast this week and $20bn over a month if the trend holds, and the buyback desk ran 1.2x 2025 average daily volume before a roughly 9/15 blackout. A JPM section reads positioning as largely neutral, with post-Jackson Hole history showing no consistent direction.
